 Maryland football vs. Illinois preview
 ﻿The Terps look to reset as interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim takes the reins for the final five games.
 by Jude Wilkenfeld Oct 30, 2026, 10:50 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Maryland football has a rare midseason clean slate after firing former head coach Mike Locksley and appointing former defensive backs coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim to an interim role.
 While changing coaches with five games left in a struggling season gives the Terps limited room to make drastic playbook and procedure changes, Abdul-Rahim has made concerted efforts to change the narrative. This week also gives Maryland a chance to win its game after the bye week, something it couldn’t do in 10 attempts under Locksley.
 ”This is a five-game season for us, and as far as I’m concerned, we’re 0-0 right now, and the kids are excited to show you guys a different or better brand of football,” Abdul-Rahim said.
 The Terps get their chance at a fresh start Saturday at SECU Stadium against Illinois. The game will begin at noon and air on FS1.
 Illinois Fighting Illini (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) 
 2025 Record: 9-4, 5-4 Big Ten 
 After capping off one of Illinois’ best seasons in recent memory with a bowl win over a ranked opponent, sixth-year head coach Bret Bielema failed to retain the talent that led its success. That failure has led to a season that can only be described as erratic.
 The Illini dropped games to Duke and Purdue early on but are now coming off consecutive wins against conference opponents. Against Michigan State, Illinois nearly choked away a 13-point halftime lead. The Illini’s 38-37 overtime win could have very easily ended in similar fashion to Locksley’s nail-in-the-coffin loss against Rutgers.
 Illinois will be missing a key link in the chain Saturday, as starting quarterback Katin Houser remains out after breaking his hand against the Spartans. This could allow Maryland’s defense, which just allowed Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan to throw for 291 yards and three touchdowns, the opportunity to take advantage of an inexperienced passer.
 Players to watch 
 Michael Clayton II, freshman quarterback, No. 7 — However, with Houser out last week against then-No. 25 Oregon, Clayton provided Bielema a huge sigh of relief. The quarterback completed 11 of 18 passes for 84 yards and two touchdowns in his first-ever start and earned Big Ten Freshman of the Week honors for his efforts.
 While Illinois’ playcalling didn’t allow him to fully showcase his arm talent, his pocket mobility may be enough to startle Maryland’s defense.
 Collin Dixon, senior wide receiver, No. 17 — Providing Clayton with a safety net as he continues to adjust to Big Ten football is the senior wide receiver from Ohio. Dixon leads the conference with 54 receptions and ranks third with just under 100 receiving yards per game. He also ranks fourth nationally in receiving touchdowns, just behind Jeremiah Smith, Jesse Legree and Malachi Toney.
 Aidan Laughery, fifth-year running back, No. 21 — Any player would feel pressure to perform with a nickname like “The Flatland Flash,” but Laughery has taken it in stride. His blistering straight-line speed and low center of gravity have propelled him to a conference second-best 6.9 yards per carry. His skill set could give the Terps trouble given their issues containing UCLA’s running backs earlier this season.
 Strength 
 Chunk plays. While Illinois sits firmly in the middle of the pack, its ability to connect on long-yardage scenarios should be another confounding variable for Maryland. The Illini average 6.4 yards per play — the fifth-best mark in the Big Ten — and have found success against a number of the conference’s best defenses; Illinois logged eight plays of over 20 yards against Ohio State, a team the Terps only mustered 149 total yards against.
 Weakness 
 Air defense. While Maryland’s secondary has faced consistent struggles this season, the Illini are one of the worst Power Four teams at defending passes. Illinois allows 248 air yards per game, which is good for the second-highest mark in the conference. That could be explained by poor defensive line pressure and growing pains associated with former defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck’s scheme during his brief stint. Terp quarterback Malik Washington could take the top off the Illini defense coming off a refreshing performance facing the Scarlet Knights.
 Three things to watch 
 1. Can Maryland break the bye week curse? Under Locksley, Maryland went an abysmal 0-10 following bye weeks, a trend that goes against everything the Saturday off is supposed to provide. As a program, Maryland has lost 12 straight games following a bye. Abdul-Rahim has his first chance to redirect the program against Illinois by eliminating one of the many ugly streaks that took place under his predecessor.
 2. Offensive package changes. While no staff changes took place on the offensive side following the firing, offensive coordinator Clint Trickett’s importance has only grown. Abdul-Rahim said that the offense would transition to a simpler, more situation-driven package on Saturday but threw his full support behind Trickett as the lead playcaller.
 “I think he does a great job. I think he has a very innovative mind,” Abdul-Rahim said.
 3. Can new beginnings draw a crowd? After selling out SECU Stadium for the Virginia Tech game, Maryland has been unable to attract the masses to recent home contests. If the prospects of a new head coach and an early start before Halloween festivities weren’t enough, the Terps have put a potentially life-changing offer on the table in hopes of boosting second-half student section retention.
